title: Birational pullback preserves line-bundle degree on proper integral curves
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ and $X'$ be integral schemes proper over $k$, each of topological Krull dimension one [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $f:X'\to X$ be a morphism over $k$ that induces an isomorphism between dense open subschemes of $X'$ and $X$. For every invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module], its pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] satisfies
$$\deg_k(f^*L)=\deg_k(L),$$
where on either proper curve $Z$ the degree is $\deg_k(M)=\chi(Z,M)-\chi(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle, def-pc-euler-characteristic]. No smoothness of either curve and no algebraic-closedness of $k$ are required.

source.place: Tag 0AYU, label lemma-degree-birational-pullback, rank-one specialization for integral proper curves.

proof.text: Both structure morphisms are separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. A field is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$; thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ and $X'$ Noetherian. The given isomorphism of dense opens sends the generic point of $X'$ to that of $X$ and identifies their local rings: these points exist by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober], lie in every nonempty open by irreducibility, and open restriction leaves their stalks unchanged. In particular $f$ is dominant and induces an isomorphism of function fields. Since $X'$ is proper over $k$ and $X$ separated over $k$, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] makes $f$ proper. All hypotheses of [lem-trf-proper-birational-curve-finite] now hold: both schemes are integral separated finite-type curves of dimension one, and the proper dominant map identifies their function fields. Consequently $f$ is finite.

source.place: Tag 0AYU, lemma-degree-birational-pullback, opening finiteness reduction; Tags 01W6, 01T6 and 0AB7 (lemma-finite-in-codim-1).

proof.text: Set $F=f_*\mathcal O_{X'}$. The structure sheaves and $L$ are quasi-coherent of finite type: locally they are free of rank one, by [def-sc-invertible-module]. Hence they are coherent by [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], using the Noetherianness from Step 1. The pullback $f^*L$ is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor], so it too is coherent. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent], $F$ and $f_*f^*L$ are coherent on $X$. Let $Q$ be the cokernel of the structure map $u:\mathcal O_X\to F$. Then $Q$ is coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum].

source.place: Tags 01XZ (lemma-coherent-Noetherian), 01Y6 (lemma-finite-pushforward-coherent), with Modules Tag 01BY (lemma-coherent-abelian); the coherent defect of 0AYU.

proof.text: The map $u$ is injective, and its generic stalk is an isomorphism. To check this explicitly, let $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be a nonempty affine open of $X$. Finiteness [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] gives $f^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $B$ finite over $A$. The inverse image is nonempty because $f$ is dominant. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $A$ and $B$ inject into their generic fields. Step 1 identifies these fields as $K$, compatibly with $A\to B$; hence $A\to B$ is injective. Moreover, for $S=A\setminus\{0\}$, $S^{-1}B$ is a subring of $K$ containing $S^{-1}A=K$, so $S^{-1}B=K$. The affine description of $F$ in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] identifies its generic stalk with this localization. Thus $Q_\eta=0$, where $\eta$ is the generic point of $X$, and the defining cokernel sequence is $0\to\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{u}F\to Q\to0$.

source.place: Tag 0AYU, lemma-degree-birational-pullback, kernel and cokernel at generic points; integral specialization has zero kernel. Affine generic-field description: Tags 01RV and 01HV.

proof.text: By [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], the coherent $Q$ is quasi-coherent of finite type. Its support is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-support], whose clause (3) identifies it with the image of a closed immersion. Step 3 says it omits $\eta$, so it is a proper closed subset of $X$. It has dimension at most zero by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]: a strict chain of two nonempty irreducible closed subsets inside this support, followed by the integral closed subset $X$, would give a chain of length two in the one-dimensional $X$. The empty support also has dimension at most zero. We may therefore apply [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support] to $Q$ and $L$, obtaining $\chi(X,Q\otimes L)=\chi(X,Q)$, with $Q\otimes L$ coherent.

source.place: Tag 0AYU, zero-dimensional defect; Tag 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite), rank-one case, with Morphisms Tag 05JU.

proof.text: Here is the needed rank-one projection formula without a derived assertion. The local bilinear maps $s\otimes b\mapsto (f^*s)b$, formed from [def-pc-module-pullback] and [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], give a sheaf map $\theta:L\otimes F\to f_*f^*L$. On a trivializing open $V$ for $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module], choose a basis $e$. Then $f^*e$ is a basis on $f^{-1}V$ by the tensor definition of pullback, and $\theta$ is the identity $F|_V\to F|_V$, sending $e\otimes b$ to $b f^*e$. On overlaps a change $e'=ae$, with $a$ a unit, multiplies both formulas by $f^*a$; thus these local descriptions agree. The resulting global map is an isomorphism because its restrictions to this cover have inverses.

source.place: Tag 01E8, lemma-projection-formula (in Section 01E6), ordinary degree-zero rank-one case; its local-trivialization argument is written out.

proof.text: Tensor the short exact sequence of Step 3 with $L$. Exactness can be checked on the trivializing cover from Step 5, where tensoring with $L$ is the identity on modules and maps. Thus $0\to L\to L\otimes F\to L\otimes Q\to0$ is exact. This uses only the locally free rank-one definition [def-sc-invertible-module] and the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. In particular, the middle term is coherent by the isomorphism of Step 5 and the coherence in Step 2, and the last term is coherent by Step 4 (or by the same local trivializations).

source.place: Tag 0AYU, tensoring the defect sequence by the locally free sheaf; rank-one exactness checked locally.

proof.text: The finite morphism $f$ is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] to the quasi-coherent modules $\mathcal O_{X'}$ and $f^*L$. For every $i\ge0$ it identifies $H^i(X,F)$ with $H^i(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ and $H^i(X,f_*f^*L)$ with $H^i(X',f^*L)$. These identifications are $k$-linear: the edge maps are linear over $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and $f$ is a $k$-morphism. All these coherent cohomology groups are finite-dimensional and vanish in sufficiently large degree by [lem-pc-coherent-hi], applied to the proper structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Taking their alternating dimensions [def-pc-euler-characteristic], and using Step 5, gives $\chi(X,F)=\chi(X',\mathcal O_{X'})$ and $\chi(X,L\otimes F)=\chi(X',f^*L)$.

source.place: Tag 0AYU, first and last equalities, using Cohomology of Schemes Tag 089W (lemma-relative-affine-cohomology) and Tags 02O5, 02O6.

proof.text: Apply the short-exact-sequence clause of [lem-pc-euler-additive] to the coherent sequences in Steps 3 and 6. It gives $\chi(X,F)=\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)+\chi(X,Q)$ and $\chi(X,L\otimes F)=\chi(X,L)+\chi(X,L\otimes Q)$. In Step 4, [lem-pc-chi-zero-dim-support] gave $\chi(X,Q\otimes L)=\chi(X,Q)$; the tensor symmetry follows directly by $q\otimes s\mapsto s\otimes q$ from [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], so $\chi(X,L\otimes Q)=\chi(X,Q)$ as well. Substitute these identities and Step 7, then subtract: $\chi(X',f^*L)-\chi(X',\mathcal O_{X'})=\chi(X,L)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$.

source.place: Tag 0AYU, Euler-characteristic calculation with n=1; Tags 08AA (lemma-euler-characteristic-additive) and 0AYT (lemma-chi-tensor-finite).

proof.text: By [def-pc-degree-line-bundle], the left side of the equality in Step 8 is $\deg_k(f^*L)$ and its right side is $\deg_k(L)$. The pullback is invertible by Step 2, and both curves are proper over the same original field $k$, so these are precisely the two degrees in the statement. This proves the assertion without any smoothness or algebraic-closedness hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 0AYU, conclusion, using the degree definition (Tag 0BEW, definition-degree).
